original_question: What is the name of the deadly condition that results from a failure in the proper maturation of the midline mesoderm and ventral body wall (chest) during embryonic development, causing the heart to be abnormally located either partially or entirely outside the thorax?

final_qi.question: What is the name of the deadly condition that results from a failure in the proper maturation of the midline mesoderm and ventral body wall (chest) during embryonic development, causing the heart to be abnormally located either partially or entirely outside the thorax?
final_qi.long_answer: Ectopia cordis is a rare, usually lethal congenital malformation in which incomplete fusion of the midline mesoderm and ventral thoracic wall during embryogenesis leaves the sternum and pericardium defective. As a result, the heart develops outside the thoracic cavity—sometimes entirely, sometimes partially—exposing it to external injury and causing profound cardiorespiratory compromise.
